steps.text: Part 5 of 5: Your first moves: three habits. This part covers Check yourself. Each part is short on purpose: finish one, play a game or take a break, and come back.

steps.prompt: Optional: play a short game as White from the start. Try to take the centre, develop a piece each move, and castle, and watch for the moment your opponent makes a threat.
Explain to a friend in three sentences why we start with a centre pawn, bring out a piece each move, and castle. Name one case where you would not.

steps.text: **One possible answer.** A centre pawn takes space and frees a bishop and the queen. A new piece each move gets the army working before the fighting starts, and castling tucks the king away while the rook joins in. I would skip a habit when something is threatened, such as a mate threat on f7, because answering the threat comes first.

steps.prompt: In the questions you just did, what did you check first: a threat against you, a piece to develop, or castling? Name the piece or square that decided it for you.

steps.caption: Look again, from an earlier part of this lesson. A quiet game of the Italian opening, move by move.

line.say: Habit one: a centre pawn takes space and frees the bishop and the queen.
A knight comes out toward the centre and attacks the pawn on e5.
Black develops a knight and guards the pawn.
The bishop comes out and aims at the pawn on f7.
Black mirrors the move and aims at f2.
A modest pawn move supports the centre pawn and opens a path for the bishop on c1.
The second knight comes out and attacks the pawn on e4.
White castles: the king is safe in the corner and the rook is closer to the centre.
Black supports its centre pawn and opens the bishop on c8.
White gets ready to push the d-pawn, which would give it two centre pawns. [I]
Black castles too. Both kings are safe. White has one knight out and Black two; the knight on b1 still has to join. [I]

steps.text: **Remember.** Three habits: a centre pawn, a new piece each move, then castle. Before using them, ask yourself: is anything threatened? If so, answer the threat first, because the habits are for quiet moments.
